newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mediation underway in Tsumeb mine strike.
newsitem.headline: Mediation underway in Tsumeb mine strike.

text.p: Mediation efforts commenced on Wednesday morning to try to resolve a five-week-old strike at Tsumeb Corp Ltd (TCL) in Namibia, owner Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said.

A spokesman declined to comment on the progress of the talks between management and the Mineworkers' Union of Namibia (MUN) but told Reuters from Namibia that discussions were likely to continue on Thursday.
The mines and smelters have been shut down since August 23 when MUN members went on strike over pay.
The company said last week that the Tsumeb mine was flooding. Pumping at the two other mines of Kombat and Otjihase was satisfactory.
TCL has started repairs on the copper smelter, damaged by strikers at the start of the dispute. The work is expected to take until early November.
The strike is costing TCL some 80 tonnes a day in lost copper production and a similar amount in lost lead.
The lead smelter appeared undamaged, but will still take around two weeks to restart.
TCL produced just under 30,000 tonnes of blister copper last year and 27,000 tonnes of lead. Most of the lead was produced from bought-in material while copper output was from TCL mines.
